### The family as recorded

Jean Baptiste Moreau was born 12 March 1821 in Bastogne (Luxembourg Province) and died 3 October 1889 in the same place. The tree shows him as the father of two children — Henri Moreau (born 1848) and Josephine Moreau (born 1851) — alongside Marie Dubois (born 1825), who is listed as the other parent of both children. Three records are attached to Jean Baptiste: a civil registration birth entry, a church baptism record, and a household census entry from 1866. Each of the other three family members has only one record apiece, all civil registration birth entries.

### Error found

**The 1821 birth is attributed to a country that didn't exist yet.** Jean Baptiste's birth is recorded under the "Belgium" jurisdiction, but Belgium did not become an independent country until 1830 — nine years after he was born. In 1821, Bastogne was part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The civil registration collection that covers this record spans 1796–1910 (civil registration started there under French rule), so the *record itself* is real and valid — but the jurisdictional label "Belgium" applied to an 1821 event is anachronistic. This doesn't mean the birth record is wrong, but it means the place label needs care: any documents from before 1830 belong to the Netherlands period, not the Belgian one.

1. **No marriage record and no couple relationship in FamilySearch.** Jean Baptiste and Marie Dubois appear together only as co-parents — there is no marriage entry, no marriage date or place, and FamilySearch has no formal "couple" link between them at all. ### Historical context to keep in mind

The Luxembourg Province of Belgium sits at the crossroads of several political transitions: French Empire rule (civil registration from 1796), then the Kingdom of the Netherlands (1815–1830), then independent Belgium (1830 onward). Jean Baptiste was born and apparently lived his entire life in this region, but his early life records belong to the Netherlands period. Church records would run alongside civil registration throughout, which is why both a civil registration entry and a church baptism record exist for his birth — that overlap is normal and expected for this time and place.
